documents.unit: Office of the Vice Provost for Academic Excellence
documents.title: Guidance on AI
documents.summary: Campus guidance that sets no AI rule itself. It points to the student code of conduct, which gives instructors authority to define unauthorized assistance, and urges instructors to state expectations and discuss them. It offers many assignment-redesign strategies and encourages experimentation within legal and ethical limits.
documents.stance_why: The page says the code of conduct "gives the instructor authority over defining unauthorized assistance, authorized sources, and specifically prohibited behavior", and only "strongly encouraged" instructors to be specific; no campus ban or permission is set, so the decision is delegated.

units.why: The opening names benefits: "personalize learning experiences" and tailored support. It is a statement of benefits, not a rule, so informs and P87.
units.anchor: AI-powered tools can provide new learning modes, personalize learning experiences

units.why: Says AI "can streamline administrative tasks, enhancing efficiency"; a benefit claim, not a rule, so P87 (no administrative-rule type fits since nothing is required).
units.anchor: AI can streamline administrative tasks, enhancing efficiency and potentially reducing operational costs
units.fit_note: Benefit is for administration rather than learning.

units.why: Lists "data privacy, ethics, algorithmic bias" as concerns that integration raises; a concern statement, informs, closest to P53 (bias and harms).
units.anchor: raises important questions about data privacy, ethics, algorithmic bias
units.frag_start: However, the integration of AI also
units.fit_note: Also names data privacy and the need for faculty and staff preparation.

units.why: The code of conduct clause on "Cheating, plagiarism, or other forms of academic dishonesty" is cited as the basis for AI integrity, so it frames misuse as an integrity matter. It does not name AI itself, so P36 fits only partly.
units.anchor: Cheating, plagiarism, or other forms of academic dishonesty.
units.frag_start: The UHM student code of conduct (IV.B.1.a)
units.fit_note: The text does not mention AI explicitly; the section heading "AI and Academic Integrity" ties it to AI.

units.why: "gives the instructor authority over defining unauthorized assistance" places the AI rule with each instructor, so P04 not P36.
units.anchor: gives the instructor authority over defining unauthorized assistance, authorized sources, and specifically prohibited behavior

units.why: "strongly encouraged to: Be specific about expectations and limitations on student use of AI" tells instructors to state AI expectations, a should; P09 over P66 because it is about stating the rule in assignments.
units.anchor: Be specific about expectations and limitations on student use of AI in assignments
units.fit_note: Applies to assignments, not only the syllabus.

units.why: Instructors are encouraged to "Hold students responsible for the accuracy of facts and sources", an accountability duty on AI output; P31 is nearest.
units.anchor: Hold students responsible for the accuracy of facts and sources used in assignments
units.frag_start: Hold students responsible for the accuracy
units.fit_note: Framed as instructors holding students responsible; does not say AI output is often wrong.

units.why: "Talk through scenarios with classes to provide clarity on expectations" asks instructors to discuss AI rules with students, matching P66.
units.anchor: Talk through scenarios with classes to provide clarity on expectations

units.why: "Syllabi and class discussions should make instructor expectations clear with respect to use of AI tools" is a should about stating AI expectations; P09 fits.
units.anchor: should make instructor expectations clear with respect to use of AI tools
units.frag_start: Syllabi and class discussions should make

units.why: "UHOIC maintains sample statements for adaptation" supports instructors with ready syllabus language; it is faculty support, P63.
units.anchor: UHOIC maintains
units.policy: UHOIC maintains sample statements for adaptation in a syllabus or specific assignments.
units.fit_note: Support is sample statements rather than workshops.

units.why: Says assignments "may need redesign to achieve our learning objectives", a call to redesign around AI, P35.
units.anchor: assignments and assessments may need redesign to achieve our learning objectives
units.frag_start: The widespread availability of AI tools creates

units.why: Recommends to "Chunk assignments with due dates for individual elements" such as outlines and drafts; redesign strategy, P35.
units.anchor: Chunk assignments with due dates for individual elements
units.frag_end: notes on research articles, and drafts.

units.why: Suggests instructors review "Google Docs version history and/or draftback" to see writing progression, process evidence to identify misuse; P40.
units.anchor: Google Docs version history and/or

units.why: Suggests to "Replace a writing assignment with an audio file, podcast, video" so that relying on AI is "more work than it is worth"; assignment redesign, P35.
units.anchor: Replace a writing assignment with an audio file

units.why: "Incorporate AI. Ask students to generate a ChatGPT response" and analyze it; AI built into an assignment as a redesign, so P35 (P79 requires AI use but this is an example of one redesign).
units.anchor: Ask students to generate a ChatGPT response to a question of their own choosing
units.frag_end: strengths and weaknesses of the response.

units.why: "Reference class materials or sources that are not available on the internet" is an assignment design tactic against AI answers, P35.
units.anchor: sources that are not available on the internet

units.why: "Include visuals" that students respond to is another redesign tactic, P35.
units.anchor: images or videos that students need to respond to
units.frag_end: videos that students need to respond to

units.why: "Connect to current events or conversations in your field" is a redesign tactic, P35.
units.anchor: current events or conversations in your field

units.why: "Ask for application of personal knowledge/experience" is a redesign tactic, P35.
units.anchor: application of personal knowledge

units.why: "Employ authentic and contextualized assessments" so "it is challenging for students to rely solely on AI"; redesign, P35.
units.anchor: authentic and contextualized assessments
units.frag_end: rely solely on AI for complete solutions

units.why: "Use open-ended questions" less likely to be answered by AI, redesign, P35.
units.anchor: open-ended questions
units.frag_end: encouraging engagement in original thinking and reflection

units.why: "Incorporate elements that evaluate the process students followed", with explanations or reflections alongside submissions, checks understanding; P34 nearest.
units.anchor: evaluate the process students followed
units.frag_end: individual thought processes and learning journeys
units.fit_note: Written explanations and reflections submitted with work, not interviews or oral checks.

units.why: Points to an "annotated listing maintained by UHOIC" of AI teaching resources, faculty support, P63.
units.anchor: annotated listing maintained by
units.fit_note: A resource list rather than workshops.

units.why: "Teaching and learning about AI is one piece of a need to assist students" in digital skills casts AI as a skill; P44.
units.anchor: Teaching and learning about AI is one piece of a need to assist students
units.frag_start: Experts agree that generative AI tools

units.why: "Faculty and students are encouraged to experiment with AI tools" within legal and ethical limits, a welcome of AI use; P02.
units.anchor: encouraged to experiment with AI tools
units.fit_note: Encouragement to experiment is conditioned on staying within legal and ethical parameters.

units.why: "university personnel should be aware of policies and procedures that relate to the adoption of new technologies" listing EP 2.219, 2.215, 2.210; P77 comply with existing policy.
units.anchor: university personnel should be aware of policies and procedures that relate to the adoption
units.fit_note: Awareness duty rather than a compliance mandate; policies cover data protection and IT use.

units.why: Points to "UH Approved 3rd-Party Online Tools" as the list personnel should know; P92 use approved tools, though stated only as a pointer.
units.anchor: Approved 3rd-Party Online Tools
units.fit_note: A pointer to the approved-tools list, not an explicit duty to use only those tools.

notes: Single included document. Many units are P35 redesign tactics, coded one per tactic. No school or computing document found.
